data.narrative:
Inertia Enterprises is a Series A nuclear energy company that has raised $450M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 11 total companies across the nuclear sector—3 public names (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private firms, with direct peers including Fuse Energy, Helion, Oklo, Valar Atomics, and X-Energy at comparable or adjacent funding stages.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis used the $450M total raised as a valuation proxy and applied a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A advancement, yielding $900M. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—Valar Atomics ($6.0B, Series B), Nano Nuclear Energy ($808M, Seed), and Fuse Energy ($200M, Series A)—produced a median of $808M, with a range spanning $200M to $6.0B. The wide dispersion reflects stage and technology maturity variation within the nuclear venture landscape.

Triangulating these two methods produces a valuation range of $687M (low) to $1.0B (high), with a median of $854M. This range reflects material uncertainty around Inertia's relative positioning versus the peer set. Key variables affecting placement within the band include capital efficiency relative to Fuse Energy, technology differentiation versus Valar Atomics' later-stage valuation, and execution risk in the Series A-to-B transition.
